clue.text: A man of means-and to top it a heel!

parts.note: to cap something is to top it
taken as written
a ship that heels over lists

explanation.surface: A sneer at a rich man: on top of everything else, he is a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' looks like the cad of the surface; here it is the verb, a ship heeling or listing to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitalist is someone with wealth invested in business, a person of substantial means.

clue.text: A hold-up caused by the number-one man

parts.note: a dam holds up the flow of water

explanation.surface: A delay caused by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he was the first man created.

clue.text: Popular nurse, though mean

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: A popular nurse who is nonetheless mean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like the adjective stingy; it is the verb, to have in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to have the purpose of doing it.

clue.text: Helped a five and suffered for it

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ailed means was ill, suffered

explanation.surface: Someone helped a five-person team and paid for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something availed if it was of use or benefit.

clue.text: The Greek character in the trio talked of escaping

indicators.note: letters escaping from inside these words form a run within them

explanation.surface: A Greek man in a trio said to have escaped.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A soldier's dog

definitions.meaning: a member of the British Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve
a small breed of hunting dog

explanation.surface: A soldier's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A member of the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, is called by this nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Territorial Army volunteers have this nickname, and it also names a breed of small hunting dog.

clue.text: Articles about lean lines appearing in New Zealand

indicators.note: the articles go around the other pieces

parts.note: an and an are two indefinite articles
to tip is to lean or tilt
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Newspaper articles about thin lines seen in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like an adjective, thin; it is the verb, to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: From the British viewpoint, Australia and New Zealand lie on the opposite side of the globe.

clue.text: Skilled worker giving unusual names to his offspring

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a son is offspring

explanation.surface: A tradesman who gives his children odd names.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who cuts and dresses building stone.

clue.text: Fly some flag, naturally

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A remark that a flag naturally flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged insect, one kind of fly.

clue.text: A person with much experience in the teaching of history?

definitions.text: A person with much experience in the teaching of history?

parts.words: A person with much experience in the teaching of history?
parts.note: an expert is read literally as a teacher whose subject is bygone times

explanation.surface: Describing a veteran history teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert or adept in some field is called this; split, it reads as a teacher of what has gone by.

clue.text: Singer made to give up

indicators.note: the singer is made into something else, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocalist forced to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a post or a game is to quit it formally.

clue.text: C division of the county

definitions.meaning: C is the Roman numeral for one more than ninety-nine
historically an English county was split into subdivisions of this name, each with its own court

explanation.surface: Part of a county labelled C.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman numeral C stands for the number; separately, old English shires were divided into administrative areas bearing the same name.

clue.text: Gets outside right a T-shirt with sovereign, they gather

indicators.note: this piece is placed outside the others

parts.note: has means gets or receives
a vest is an undershirt, a T-shirt
ER is the royal cipher of the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A busy instruction about a shirt bearing the royal emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Reapers or combines collect the crops at harvest time.

clue.text: Constituents of the Tory now, and that's significant

indicators.note: the letters of these words are the parts from which the answer is built in a new order

explanation.surface: Tory voters now matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' suggests voters in a seat; here it means the component letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth remarking on is notable, important.

clue.text: The artist when very old retired to thesouth

indicators.note: going back, retiring, reads the word backwards

parts.note: aged means very old
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: An elderly painter retired to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' means going back, so the word for very old is read backwards; 'when' and 'to' are links, and the south sits below it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was the French impressionist painter of ballet dancers.

clue.text: Act through a group of scholars

parts.note: per means through or by, as in per post
a form is a class of pupils in a British school

explanation.surface: Putting on a play by means of a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To act a part on stage is to play or present it before an audience.

clue.text: A certain weight of coin

definitions.meaning: a unit of weight of sixteen ounces
the British unit of currency, once a gold sovereign and now a coin

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the imperial unit of sixteen ounces and Britain's currency unit, now a coin.

clue.text: A theatricalsetting

parts.note: the scenery and furnishing of a stage set, the look of a production

explanation.definitionFit: The scenery and furnishings that make up a stage picture are its design or setting.

clue.text: To do with imbibing at speed

indicators.note: something drinking in another holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: re means concerning, to do with

explanation.surface: Something about drinking quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate is a pace or velocity, as in a rate of knots.

clue.text: The French like areas of grassland

parts.note: le is a French word for the
as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: The French are fond of meadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Leas are meadows or pasture, open fields of grass.

clue.text: Refreshment for the guy on the beat

definitions.text: Refreshment for the guy on the beat

parts.words: Refreshment for the guy on the beat
parts.note: a hot steam room where bathers beat themselves with birch twigs, read as if a policeman on his rounds wanted a drink

explanation.surface: Something to refresh a patrolling policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the beat' suggests a constable's patrol; in a Finnish steam bath the bather is beaten with birch twigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finnish steam bath refreshes the bather, who traditionally beats the skin with birch switches.

clue.text: Make a song about a hole being offensive

indicators.note: this piece goes around the other

parts.note: to sing is to make a song
a pit is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: Complaining that a hole in the road is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a song about' looks like the idiom to make a fuss; split, it is singing wrapped around a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting out of spite is deliberately hurting or offending someone.

clue.text: Dicky, a driver, achieved sue cess

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver with a weak heart nonetheless succeeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky', British slang for weak or unsound (a dicky heart), signals the anagram; 'sue cess' is the newspaper's misprint of success.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has made it has reached success.

clue.text: Covers the main points about strike

to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: Main points of a dispute about industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it is the verb to hit; the main points are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To enwrap something is to wrap it up or envelop it, covering it all over.

clue.text: Worn and dilapidated, but used

indicators.note: something dilapidated is broken down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something old and worn, but still in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Resources drawn on have been tapped or made use of.

clue.text: Turn pale when cut by it

indicators.note: one word is cut open and the other placed in the gap

explanation.surface: Someone blanches when wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To blanch is to lose colour, become paler.

clue.text: The economy, calls for some growth

definitions.meaning: a plant, the sea pink, which grows on cliffs and coasts

explanation.surface: A remark that the economy needs to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is economic news; the second sense is a plant, the sea pink, a 'growth' in the gardener's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful saving is economy, and the sea pink is a coastal plant of the same name.

clue.text: Taking over the church at one time

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece is placed above the other

parts.note: on means taking, as of a drug
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Seizing control of the church some time ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, in the past.

clue.text: Suffices for some animals

definitions.meaning: it will do means it is enough

explanation.definitionFit: It will do means it is enough; separately, female deer or rabbits share the plural spelling.

clue.text: Hostelry getting approval for modernisation

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry, a pub with rooms
an ovation is applause showing approval

explanation.surface: A pub being praised for its refurbishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Introducing something new is modernisation or novelty.

clue.text: Russian leaders have little time for the industrial heart of Germany

parts.note: the leading two letters of the word Russian
hr is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: Russian leaders have little time for German industry.
explanation.definitionFit: The region around the Essen and Dortmund coalfields is Germany's traditional industrial heartland.

clue.text: The eagerness to acquire designers models all round the Orient

indicators.note: the reshaped letters surround the other piece
to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: the Orient is the east, E

explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' looks like fashion models; it is the verb, reshaping DESIGNERS into an order that holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive eagerness to get more and more.
